items.title: [carbonbrief.org] El Niño-linked fires lift total carbon emissions despite fossil fuel dip
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

El Niño-related peat fires and forest degradation in Southeast Asia are projected to push land-use carbon emissions higher in 2026, bringing total global CO₂ emissions to 43.3 billion tonnes even as fossil-fuel emissions edge down, according to the Global Carbon Project’s annual assessment. The researchers link the rise in land-use emissions to drier conditions and fires often ignited by human activity. The 21st Global Carbon Budget, published Nov. 10 in Earth System Science Data and presented during the U.N. climate conference in Antalya, projects 5.1 billion tonnes of emissions from land-use change this year. The projected decline in fossil-fuel emissions is partly attributable to the Iran conflict’s energy shock, alongside the growing contribution of solar, wind and electric vehicles. The report says the land carbon sink recovered in 2025 after weakening during the 2023-24 El Niño, but the strong 2026 El Niño is expected to weaken it again in 2027. Separately, an analysis of Chinese data found that emissions fell 3.1% in July-September, the country’s steepest quarterly drop since pandemic lockdowns in 2022.

items.title: [stpetersburg.usf.edu] Study finds drought could cut cactus habitat by 80% by 2100
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

An international research team analyzed nearly 1,000 cactus species and found that more than a quarter could lose at least 80% of their suitable habitat by 2100 if severe droughts intensify. The researchers added drought projections to climate models, which commonly use long-term temperature and rainfall averages, and combined them with biodiversity records, field observations and community-science data. The projected losses could qualify affected species as Critically Endangered under criteria set by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), more than doubling the number of cacti in that category. Researchers say drought may also reduce growth or flowering without immediately killing plants, compounding threats from habitat destruction and illegal collection. The findings are expected to inform updated IUCN Red List assessments; the team says further research is needed to determine which life stages and biological processes drought affects.

items.title: [thesouthafrican.com] WMO warns strengthening El Niño could intensify global extremes into 2027
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says a strengthening El Niño could reach record strength by December and intensify heat and disruptive rainfall patterns into 2027. In its 2026 climate update, the agency reported that global temperatures from January through September averaged about 1.47°C above the preindustrial level and said 2026 is on track to rank among the four warmest years on record. Human-caused warming is adding to the risks associated with the naturally occurring climate pattern. The World Health Organization (WHO) has classified the expected health effects as an emergency for the first time for an El Niño event and published a plan for a Grade 3 preparedness response requiring major to maximal efforts. The agency warns that heat, drought and heavy rain can increase risks of heat illness, food insecurity and infectious disease, with vulnerable and conflict-affected communities facing particular danger. The WMO says the event is on track to reach record strength by December; its climate update uses data through September and does not include the latest impacts.

items.title: [nbcchicago.com] IRS raises 2027 tax brackets and child credit limits
items.content_html:

The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income tax bracket thresholds for 2027, allowing taxpayers to earn more before entering a higher bracket. Tax rates remain unchanged, with the top rate still 37%. For single filers, the 22% bracket starts above $52,025 and the 37% bracket above $661,375; for married couples filing jointly, those thresholds are $104,050 and $793,650. The IRS also increased the maximum child tax credit to $2,300, including a refundable portion of up to $1,800, and raised the maximum earned income tax credit for qualifying families with at least three children to $8,496. The annual inflation adjustments are intended to keep wage increases from pushing taxpayers into higher brackets when their purchasing power has not increased.

Results reported Nov. 16 from two phase 3 trials showed substantial reductions in body mass index (BMI) with semaglutide in children aged 6 to 11 with obesity and tirzepatide in adolescents aged 12 to 17. After 68 weeks, children receiving semaglutide had a 13.5% BMI decrease, compared with a 2.7% increase among those receiving placebo; in the 72-week teen trial, tirzepatide produced a 19-percentage-point greater BMI reduction than placebo. Both studies also recorded improvements in cardiometabolic measures, while gastrointestinal side effects were common. Ania Jastreboff, a Yale obesity researcher, said results from 26 weeks off treatment are expected in the coming months.
